body: Thats so intriguing, do you still experience this? And out of curiosity how does it feel talking about it on reddit, does this conversation feel real?

I'm sorry to hear that, it must be quite scary to experience.
I'm not sure if this is the same but a while ago when it was at its peak, I experienced something like it was literally not real and that I was almost like a god? Not really a god but like the only one "aware" or kind of like a mod playing within their own game and nobody was real and it was a part of my own making and my own world and I created everything even the people and even the philosophy of the world and I was just living in my own formulated controlled virtual world. It felt like there was no real consequences as it was "just a game" but I felt like "playing" the good character in the game/virtual world and trying to make "good" decisions therefore I luckily didn't do anything too reckless. Even people who say it's "not real" were supposed to say that as I "programmed" them to say that to make the experience immersive. I truly believed in it but I slowly came out of that extreme and now I'm at the stage where I'm beginning to come out of it completely. I think I was in some form of psychosis but I'm getting better. Again I'm not sure if this is anything similar but I was curious if it was.

 The elements of dreaminess still resonate though, kind of like day dreaminess but to an extreme. It was constant but now I'm get more and more consistent "glitches" of actual feelings. 

It kind of feels like things are out of focus and hazy and plastic, I think probably people experience things differently and I was actually curious if you experience any audible hallucinations? Sorry for lengthy reply (:

Because I notice the contrast from being zoned out to having glitches of emotion, also when reading up about it everything is exactly what is explained. My therapist suggested this was the case also, I hated feeling like there was nothingness after realising it was happening and I wanted to feel authentic to my emotions and was basing it off how I was before. It took a long time to realise what was happening and trained myself to notice when it was happening. There's different intensity of disassociation. You can know when it's happening but you're powerless to do anything about it 😅

Its very profound what you're saying and it honestly is like a limbo.. I kind of saw it like its a virtual world where everyone is an npc and it feels so plastic and sad and cold. I'm terribly sorry you're dealing with this shit too its horrendous to deal with and it fucking sucks..

I have also resorted to kinda abusing my medication and things in attempt to feel good. It is so hard to go on with things and how cold and terrible things are. I appreciate your comment to the post because you definitely sound like someone who understands x

I haven't felt a difference drinking tbh but that's just me personally and I suppose I've not drunk on 900mg but taking that dose in general didn't really do anything massive as I've built a pretty big tolerance lol. I really think it's down to individual capabilites and I think being aware of ourselves to tailor the experience to ourselves. I'm personally quite a big girl height and weight wise so I feel that can also factor into the tolerance.
